library_preparation_preflight.summary: No missing Maven dependency or Docker image is needed, but the library's real Linux code path (KeyRingAccessor via libsecret/D-Bus) can't run in headless CI without a live, unlocked Secret Service; the constructor calls verify() eagerly and will throw without one.
library_preparation_preflight.agent_guidance: CI runs only ubuntu-latest (ci.json), so the Windows (DPAPI) and macOS (KeyChainAccessor) branches of PersistenceTokenCacheAccessAspect can never be exercised here — don't try to cover them. On Linux, PersistenceTokenCacheAccessAspect's constructor branches on PersistenceSettings.isOnLinuxUseUnprotectedFileAsCacheStorage(): if false (i.e. PersistenceSettings.Builder.setLinuxKeyring(...) was used), it eagerly builds a KeyRingAccessor and calls verify() synchronously in the constructor, which does a real write/read/delete round-trip against the D-Bus Secret Service through libsecret-1 (ISecurityLibrary statically calls Native.load("libsecret-1", ...)). libsecret-1-0, dbus-daemon/dbus-run-session, and gnome-keyring-daemon are already present on the test/CI OS image, so the native library load itself will not fail — but no D-Bus session bus or unlocked keyring is running by default in a headless test process, so the verify() call will throw KeyRingAccessException and fail both the JVM and native-image test lanes. For a reliable primary test, build PersistenceSettings with setLinuxUseUnprotectedFileAsCacheStorage(true); this still exercises PersistenceTokenCacheAccessAspect's core read/write/lock logic and CacheFileAccessor/CrossProcessCacheFileLock via the normal generated scaffold with no extra setup. If coverage of the real KeyRingAccessor/libsecret/JNA path is wanted, the test's build.gradle would need a `test.doFirst` (or equivalent) that starts an ephemeral `dbus-daemon --session --fork --print-address` plus `gnome-keyring-daemon --unlock --components=secrets` (empty passphrase via stdin) and injects the resulting DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS/GNOME_KEYRING_CONTROL into the test JVM's environment before PersistenceTokenCacheAccessAspect is constructed with setLinuxKeyring(...) — this is inherently more fragile than the file-storage path, so treat it as best-effort/optional coverage rather than a hard requirement.
risks: KeyRingAccessor.verify() runs inside the PersistenceTokenCacheAccessAspect constructor, so any test that reaches the real Linux keyring path will fail outright (not just skip a feature) unless a D-Bus session + unlocked Secret Service is set up first.

ISecurityLibrary.library is a static field that calls Native.load("libsecret-1", ...) at class-init time, so merely referencing that class pays a native-library-load cost — currently satisfiable in this environment, but worth flagging as environment-dependent for native-image's JNA reflective-proxy generation.
Windows/macOS-specific code (KeyChainAccessor, DPAPI) is structurally unreachable in this repo's Linux-only CI matrix, so don't expect or chase coverage there.
